summary: Practise supplier risk mapping, grievance design, and audit protocols. Build practical human rights due diligence skills. Enquire about the course.
lede: Supply chain human rights due diligence helps procurement, legal and sustainability professionals address forced-labour risks in supplier relationships. Participants use UNGP and OECD guidance to map Tier 1 and deeper-tier risks, prioritize impacts, and assess evidence using ILO forced labour indicators. They also practise developing supplier mitigation plans, grievance and remedy pathways, risk-based audit protocols, and due diligence records, with an introduction to AI-assisted screening and its limitations.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape purchasing decisions, investigate human rights risk, or oversee supplier controls and reporting across complex supply chains.
modules: UNGPs and OECD Due Diligence Foundations
Human Rights Reporting and Action Planning
prerequisites: Working knowledge of procurement, supply chain operations, sustainability, legal, or compliance processes is recommended. No coding is required. Bring a laptop with Excel access for spreadsheet-based risk mapping and action tracking; no specialist software is required.
